samples.summary: Latched durability state is never reset when the provider is handed a different document, so one document's loss poisons every later document in the session
samples.evidence: `lost`, `persistDisabled`, `writesFailing`, `outOfSpace` and `unreportable` are `useState` latches on `DurableYorkieProvider` (lines 95, 109, 143, 146, 147) with no reset keyed on `clientKey`. The component instance is reused across documents: `CollabDocumentProvider` renders `<DurableYorkieProvider clientKey={decided.clientKey} …>` at a fixed position (collab-document-provider.tsx:365) and no call site puts a `key` on it — `board-detail.tsx:262`, `document-detail.tsx:911`, `docs-detail.tsx:353`, `slides-detail.tsx:954`, `notes-detail.tsx:380` all just pass a new `docKey` when the route param changes. So navigating /b/1 → /b/2 keeps the same instance and the same latches. After document 1 emits `local-changes-dropped` (or a single write fails), `value.durable` stays `false` forever: `useDocumentDurability()` returns false for document 2, `deriveSyncState` falls back to `not-saved` for work that *is* on disk, and `lapse` (line 215) stays `'dropped'`, so the tooltip tells the user "Earlier changes could not be reconciled, so this document is no longer being saved to this device" about a document that is being saved fine. The feature is silently dead for the rest of the session and the reported cause is wrong.

samples.summary: The recovery offer toast (`duration: Infinity`, no close button) is never dismissed after a successful recovery; clicking its action a second time reports a false error
samples.evidence: `toast.warning('Some changes could not be saved', { id: `offline-recovery-${item.id}`, duration: Infinity, … })` at offline-runtime.tsx:324. `<Toaster />` is mounted with defaults (App.tsx:193) — no `closeButton` — which the chip's own comment confirms ("the warning is `duration: Infinity` with no close button", sync-status-chip.tsx:287). Nothing ever calls `toast.dismiss('offline-recovery-…')`: the success arm at line 350 raises a *new* toast with a different id and the unmount cleanup (line 223) only sets `cancelled`, stops the watcher and closes the store. So after `recoverOfflineCopy` succeeds and `store.dropArchive(work.id)` runs (offline-copy-recovery.ts:306), the original warning stays on screen permanently with its "Save a copy" action live. A second click re-enters `recoverOfflineCopy`, `rehydrateArchive` finds no archive and returns `undefined`, so `refused: 'unreadable'` fires `toast.error('Could not recover those changes', { description: 'The stored copy could not be read.' })` — an error about work that was recovered correctly moments earlier. Contrast the chip, which deliberately retracts its own infinite toast (sync-status-chip.tsx:265, 292-297).

samples.summary: `DurableYorkieProvider` never closes the `WafflebaseDocStore` it creates, leaking an IndexedDB connection per durable editor mount
samples.evidence: `const store = useMemo(() => new WafflebaseDocStore({...}), [userId])` at durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:148 with no `useEffect` cleanup calling `store.close()`. `WafflebaseDocStore.open()` memoizes an `IDBDatabase` (`this.db`, line 534 area) that is only released by an explicit `close()` or by `onversionchange`. A grep for `.close()` across packages/frontend/src returns it only in `offline-runtime.tsx:231` and the four `offline-erase.ts` sites (345, 377, 426, 553) — never from this provider. Every unmount/remount of a durable editor (navigating between document *types*, e.g. /b/1 → /d/2, which swaps the route component) therefore abandons a live IDB connection for the life of the tab.

samples.summary: `clientKey` is swapped on an already-mounted `KeyedYorkieProvider` when navigating between documents; if the SDK does not rebuild its client on that prop change, the new document persists into the old document's store scope and will not resume
samples.evidence: `<KeyedYorkieProvider … clientKey={clientKey} store={store}>` (line 228-234) receives a new `clientKey` whenever `CollabDocumentProvider`'s `decided.clientKey` changes — which it does on every in-route document change, since the same instance is reused (no `key` at any call site). The SDK's `DocStore` is scoped `apiKey/clientKey/docKey` (see the header comment in wafflebase-doc-store.ts and `durableClientKey`, durable-session.ts). If `YorkieProvider` activates its client once in an effect that does not depend on the key, document B would be written under document A's salt, and a later direct load of B — which mints `wb:{saltB}:{userId}:{docKey}` — would find nothing to resume while the chip still reported `Saved to this device`. I could not inspect `@yorkie-js/react` (node_modules unavailable) to confirm whether it re-activates on a key change, hence the low confidence; the impact if it does not is silently unresumable local work.
searchedFor: glob node_modules/@yorkie-js/react dist typings — not present in the checkout

samples.summary: Toggling the preference off drops the per-document client-key salts while the durable client stays mounted; re-enabling in the same session writes into a scope no later session can reproduce
samples.evidence: `eraseOfflineData` calls `forgetDeviceSecret(userId)` (offline-erase.ts:39) on every path, including `watchForOfflineDisable`'s (line 607). By design the durable client is *not* torn down when the preference flips (collab-document-provider.tsx:231-255 latches the decision for the life of the open document), so it keeps its old `wb:{oldSalt}:{userId}:{docKey}`. If the user re-enables the preference before closing the document, `isPersistenceEnabled()` (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:185) starts returning true again and writes resume — into the old salt's store scope. `durableClientKey` will mint a *fresh* salt on the next page load, so those entries can never be loaded again and merely sit until the thirty-day sweep, while the chip reports the document as durable. Narrow path, but it produces exactly the unresumable-but-promised state the feature is built to avoid.

samples.summary: `deleteDocuments` dereferences the parsed body before the `?? []` guard, so a `null` JSON body turns an accepted bulk delete into a thrown TypeError
samples.evidence: `const result = (await response.json()) as { deleted: string[] }; … await purgeOfflineDocuments(result.deleted ?? []);` (documents.ts:211-215). `response.json()` on a body of literal `null` (or an empty 204-style body serialized as `null`) resolves to `null`, and `result.deleted` then throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null`. The `?? []` only covers a missing *property*, not a missing object. `assertOk` has already passed at that point, so the server has accepted the deletion and the caller sees a failure for work that succeeded. The new test only covers `okJson({})`, which has an object.

samples.summary: `RecoverableWork.documentId` is documented as "just the document id" but actually holds the type-prefixed docKey
samples.evidence: `documentIdOf` in offline-copy.ts:52 returns only the last `/` segment (`sheet-7`), while the identically-named `documentIdOf` in offline-erase.ts:390 additionally strips the type prefix (`7`). The field's doc comment at line 41 says "Just the document id, which is what routes and titles care about", and offline-copy.test.ts asserts `work.documentId` is `'note-7'`. Nothing consumes it today — `offerRecoverableWork` correctly uses `describeArchivedDocument(item.docKey).id` instead — but a future caller building a route from `documentId` would produce `/s/sheet-7`.

verdict.reason: The latches are real (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:95,109,143,146,147, lapse at 215), but the finding's mechanism — one instance reused across documents — does not hold. CollabDocumentProvider keys its held decision on `subject = ${person.id}:${docKey}` (collab-document-provider.tsx:256). When docKey changes, useDurableDocument's `answered = decision?.subject === subject` is false because `decision` is state written only from the effect (use-durable-document.ts:192-221,232), so `settled` is false (line 254) and `ready` is false (collab-document-provider.tsx:268). `held.current` still holds the old subject (only rewritten when ready, lines 269-270), so the component takes `return null` at 344-346, which unmounts DurabilityLapseScope > DurableYorkieProvider and discards all useState latches; the provider remounts fresh with the new clientKey once the election resolves. The only alternative transition (new document ineligible) renders `inner` at the same position as DurableYorkieProvider (362-383), a different element type, which also unmounts it. DurableYorkieProvider has exactly one production call site (collab-document-provider.tsx:365), so no other path re-keys a live instance. The suite confirms the boundary: the no-unmount case is the preference flip where `subject` is unchanged (collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx:205-234), while an identity change mounts a new client key (174-201). Therefore document 1's `lost`/`writesFailing`/etc. cannot leak into document 2.

verdict.reason: The code is as described: offline-runtime.tsx:324-326 raises a `duration: Infinity` warning toast with id `offline-recovery-${item.id}` and a live "Save a copy" action (330-337); nothing in the module ever calls `toast.dismiss` (the success arm at 350 opens a different toast, and the unmount cleanup at 223-232 only sets `cancelled`, stops the watcher and closes the store). `<Toaster />` is mounted bare and outside the Router (App.tsx:191-193), so such a toast persists across navigation and unmount — the repo itself documents this hazard and retracts its own Infinity toast for exactly that reason (sync-status-chip.tsx:265, 287-297). Recovery drops the archive on success (offline-copy-recovery.ts:289, 306) and a subsequent call returns `refused: 'unreadable'` (268-271), which maps to `toast.error('Could not recover those changes', { description: 'The stored copy could not be read.' })` (offline-runtime.tsx:340-347). My only doubt is that sonner 2.0.3 (package.json:79, pnpm-lock.yaml:767-769) auto-dismisses a toast after the action's onClick unless `event.preventDefault()` is called, which would neutralize the specific second-click chain; node_modules is absent so I could not read that implementation and cannot cite it as a grounded counterexample. Even if it holds, the verified non-dismissal on unmount leaves the offer on screen after sign-out with an action that re-enters recovery against a closed store (offline-runtime.tsx:231), producing the same misleading error via the catch at 366-369. Uncertainty keeps the finding.

verdict.reason: The premise — that a mounted KeyedYorkieProvider receives a changed clientKey on an in-route document change — is blocked by the pre-decision gate at collab-document-provider.tsx:344-346. clientKey is not live state: it is decided.clientKey, i.e. held.current (283-286), a ref frozen per subject and mutated only under `ready && held.current.subject !== subject` (269-270). When docKey changes, useDurableDocument's own subject embeds docKey (use-durable-document.ts:186) and answered = decision?.subject === subject (232) is necessarily false on that first render, since decision is set only from the election effect (192-221); for an eligible document settled = !eligible || answered (254) is then false, so ready is false and held.current still names the old subject — hitting `return null` (344-346), which unmounts DurableYorkieProvider and its YorkieProvider. The provider reappears only as a fresh mount once held is re-latched. The two ways to bypass that gate both preserve the invariant: (a) held.current.subject === subject means the subject is unchanged so the frozen clientKey is identical (the no-null-render case asserted in collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx:204-236); (b) ready true on a subject change requires !eligible (use-durable-document.ts:254), giving durable:false/clientKey:undefined so line 362 renders `inner` — a different element type at the position, also an unmount. Hence the SDK's re-activation behavior on a key change is not load-bearing and the claimed cross-document salt scope cannot arise by this route.

finding.summary: `saved-locally` is excluded from `mayHaveUnsent`, so the in-app navigation guard is dropped — but leaving a document detaches it, and the SDK's detach deletes the on-disk entry without archiving it
finding.evidence: `const mayHaveUnsent = stranded || state === 'saving';` (line 114) with `stranded = state === 'not-saved'` (line 78). The new `saved-locally` state therefore registers neither the `beforeunload` handler (line 125) nor `useNavigationGuard` (line 155), nor the probe (`use-unsaved-work-probe.ts:24`). For a *reload* that is correct: the entry survives and resumes. For an **in-app route change** it is not: this diff's own documentation states that `detachDocument` calls `removeFromStore` unconditionally on its success path (`packages/frontend/src/lib/wafflebase-doc-store.ts:764-771`), and `WafflebaseDocStore.remove()` archives only when `expectLoss` was latched — which happens exclusively from the `local-changes-dropped` handler (`durable-yorkie-provider.tsx` `DurableLossWatch`), never on an ordinary detach. `saved-locally` is reachable while `connected` is true (`sync-state.ts` returns it for `connected && syncFailed && durable`), where the detach RPC can succeed even though pushes are being rejected. Result: one click on a sidebar link unmounts the provider, the detach removes the only durable copy, the in-memory queue goes with it, and nothing warned the user — the exact loss the guard existed to prevent, now suppressed by the state that promises safety.

verdict.reason: The finding's central claim — that `saved-locally` registers no in-app navigation guard — is not present in the code. `sync-status-chip.tsx:144` defines `const leavingLosesWork = mayHaveUnsent || savedLocally;` and `sync-status-chip.tsx:185-186` passes `leavingLosesWork` (not `mayHaveUnsent`) as the `active` flag to `useNavigationGuard`, so a `saved-locally` document does hold back in-app route changes. The prompt even carries a dedicated `savedLocally` branch (L196-198) whose wording states precisely the hazard the reviewer describes: leaving closes the document and removes the on-disk copy. The fire-time decision is durability-independent: `useNavigationGuard` calls the guard live (use-navigation-guard.ts:54-57) and `hasUnsentEdits` is `unflushed` (use-sync-status.ts:110-113, 222), a checkpoint-vs-last-edit comparison that ignores `durable`, so the connected+syncFailed+durable route into `saved-locally` (sync-state.ts:75-85) is guarded too. Only the genuinely quoted exclusions remain: `beforeunload` (L155) and `use-unsaved-work-probe.ts:24`, both of which govern reloads — the case the reviewer concedes is correct, since the durable entry survives a reload and the next attach resumes from it. No unguarded detach/data-loss path exists as described.

finding.summary: The session-start reconcile destroys the archive of every document that was deleted upstream — the exact unsent work the recovery offer exists to hand back — before the offer is ever made.
finding.evidence: `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments()` enumerates `storedDocumentIds({ archives: true })` and, for every id not in the server listing, calls `purgeDocument(id, { archives: "drop", skipOpen: true, updatedSince: listedAt })` (offline-erase.ts:487-497). "The document was deleted or GC'd upstream" is one of the three documented causes of an archive (offline-copy.ts header), and `GET /documents` hard-deletes (`document.service.ts:126 prisma.document.delete`), so such an id can never be in `accessible`. `dropArchivesForDocument` only spares rows with `archivedAt >= updatedSince` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1031-1036) — an archive written in a *previous* session always fails that — or rows whose document is open, which a deleted document never is. And `OfflineRuntime` runs the reconcile strictly *before* `offerRecoverableWork` (offline-runtime.tsx:157 then 192), and offers only once per mount, so an archive created mid-session is first offered next session, by which time the reconcile has already deleted it. This directly contradicts the deliberate exemption on the same path: `purgeOfflineDocuments` defaults to `archives: "keep"` precisely because "'deleted upstream' is one of the three paths that produce an archive" (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:886-889). Net effect: the only durable copy of work the server never took is silently deleted, which is the loss the feature exists to prevent.

verdict.reason: The described code does not exist in the working tree. `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` does NOT pass `archives: "drop"` unconditionally: at offline-erase.ts:541-549 it computes `dropArchive = archived.has(id) && options.isRevoked ? (await options.isRevoked(id)) === true : false` and passes `archives: dropArchive ? "drop" : "keep"`, so an archive is destroyed only on a positive revocation answer and is kept by default (including when no callback is supplied or the callback throws/returns non-true). The sole caller supplies `isRevoked` (offline-runtime.tsx:103-110, wired in at :182) which returns `true` only for `HttpError.status === 403` — a document hard-deleted upstream answers 404, so its archive is preserved through the reconcile and is subsequently offered by `offerRecoverableWork` (offline-runtime.tsx:215), whose 404 branch (offline-runtime.tsx:296-303) explicitly handles the deleted-upstream case. A repo-wide grep finds no `archives: "drop"` occurrence in offline-erase.ts (only tests and a docstring in wafflebase-doc-store.ts:895). Tests at offline-erase.test.ts:556/571/584 assert the keep-by-default behavior. The ordering premise (reconcile before offer) is factually correct but harmless given the guard, so no data-loss path exists as described.

finding.summary: On the currently pinned build the chip tells every user with unsent work "This browser cannot save documents locally" — a build-time library check reported as a browser capability.
finding.evidence: `lapse` is computed as `!supportsClientKey() ? "unsupported" : ...` (collab-document-provider.tsx:291-299), and `supportsClientKey()` reads `__YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__` against `MinClientKeyVersion = "0.7.23"` (yorkie-capabilities.ts). `packages/frontend/package.json:66` pins `@yorkie-js/react` at `0.7.22`, so the predicate is false on every build shipped by this PR. The scope wraps both branches and the editor subtree, and `SyncStatusChip` renders inside it (document-detail.tsx:910-921 → SiteHeader → SyncStatusChip), so `tooltipFor(...)` appends `LAPSE_REASONS.unsupported` = "This browser cannot save documents locally." to the `not-saved` tooltip for *every* user who goes offline today — including on the share route, where the correct reason is `not-permitted`. The statement is false (it is the app build, not the browser) and it is on the commonest path the chip has.

verdict.reason: The finding's quoted code is inverted. At collab-document-provider.tsx:303-310 the ternary is `decided?.durable || !supportsClientKey() ? undefined : !permitted ? "not-permitted" : ...` — a build below MinClientKeyVersion publishes NO lapse, it does not publish "unsupported". Lines 288-302 that the finding cites as the expression are a comment explaining exactly why the unsupported case must publish nothing. Corroborating: the `DurabilityLapse` union (durable-document-context.ts:104-129) has no `"unsupported"` member (and documents its deliberate absence at 108-113), so the claimed value would not typecheck; `LAPSE_REASONS` (sync-status-tooltip.ts:35-45) has no such key; and the string "This browser cannot save documents locally" does not exist anywhere in the repository (repo-wide grep returned no matches). The share-route variant of the claim also fails, since `lapse` is `undefined` there on the current pin and `not-permitted` intentionally has no tooltip sentence (sync-status-tooltip.ts:24-27) and suppresses the offer at sync-status-chip.tsx:99.
